original_value: Proactive latency-aware adaptation is an approach for self-adaptive systems that considers both the current and anticipated adaptation needs when making adaptation decisions, taking into account the latency of the available adaptation tactics. Since this is a problem of selecting adaptation actions in the context of the probabilistic behavior of the environment, Markov decision processes (MDPs) are a suitable approach. However, given all the possible interactions between the different and possibly concurrent adaptation tactics, the system, and the environment, constructing the MDP is a complex task. Probabilistic model checking has been used to deal with this problem, but it requires constructing the MDP every time an adaptation decision is made to incorporate the latest predictions of the environment behavior. In this article, we describe PLA-SDP, an approach that eliminates that runtime overhead by constructing most of the MDP offline. At runtime, the adaptation decision is made by solving the MDP through stochastic dynamic programming, weaving in the environment model as the solution is computed. We also present extensions that support different notions of utility, such as maximizing reward gain subject to the satisfaction of a probabilistic constraint, making PLA-SDP applicable to systems with different kinds of adaptation goals.

result.paraphrase: Proactive latency-aware adaptation is a technique for self-adaptive systems that bases adaptation choices on both present and expected future needs while accounting for the latency of available tactics. Because this involves choosing actions under probabilistic environmental behavior, Markov decision processes (MDPs) are an appropriate framework. Yet building the MDP is difficult due to all possible interactions among the system, the environment, and different, potentially concurrent, adaptation tactics. Probabilistic model checking has been applied to this challenge, but it demands reconstructing the MDP at each adaptation decision so the latest environmental predictions can be included. This article introduces PLA-SDP, which removes that runtime cost by building most of the MDP offline. At runtime, the adaptation choice is obtained by solving the MDP with stochastic dynamic programming, incorporating the environment model as the solution is computed. We also describe extensions supporting different utility definitions, such as maximizing reward gain while satisfying a probabilistic constraint, which makes PLA-SDP suitable for systems with varied adaptation objectives.
